devotionals.title: God Gives the Growth
devotionals.body:
In today’s passage, Apostle Paul gently redirects the Corinthians’ attention away from their favorite leaders and back to God Himself. They had begun comparing Apollos and Paul, as though spiritual growth came from human personalities. Paul reminds them that leaders are only servants. One plants, another waters, but God alone gives the growth. This truth brings freedom. It releases us from comparison, pressure, and the need for recognition.

Here are three truths from today’s passage:

1. God’s servants are instruments, not the source. Paul and Apollos each had a role. One planted the seed, another watered it. But neither had the power to make life grow. Human leaders can teach, encourage, and guide, but only God can transform the heart. Our confidence must rest in Him alone.

2. Every role matters, but no role deserves worship. Paul refuses to compete with Apollos. Each servant will be rewarded according to their own labor. God sees faithfulness, not visibility. Whether your role feels public or hidden, your work matters when it is offered to God.

3. We are God’s field and God’s building. The church belongs to God. Our lives are His work in progress. We do not belong to personalities, movements, or platforms. We belong to the One who plants, waters, and brings every good thing to maturity.

This passage invites us to rest in God’s work. We can serve faithfully without trying to control outcomes. We can honor leaders without idolizing them. We can trust that growth comes from God, and He is faithful to complete what He begins.
devotionals.prayer: Dear Lord, please fix my eyes on You. Teach me to honor those who serve without placing them above Christ. Give me grace to be faithful in my role and trust You to bring the growth.

devotionals.title: Building on Christ
devotionals.scriptureText: For no one can lay any foundation other than the one already laid, which is Jesus Christ. 1 Corinthians 3:11
devotionals.body:
In today’s passage, Apostle Paul describes the Christian life as a building project. He had laid the foundation by preaching Christ, and others were continuing the work. But Paul gives a serious reminder: the foundation is already fixed. No one can build on anything other than Jesus Christ. The question is not whether we are building, but what we are building with.

Here are three truths from today’s passage:

1. Christ is the only foundation that can hold our lives. Success, approval, relationships, and achievement cannot carry the weight of our identity. They shift and eventually fail. Jesus alone is steady, eternal, and strong enough to support everything God is building in us.

2. The quality of our work matters to God. Paul compares our work to gold, silver, costly stones, wood, hay, and straw. Some things endure; others disappear under testing. God is not only concerned with how much we do but with the motives, obedience, and faithfulness behind what we build.

3. God will test what we build. The Day will reveal the quality of each person’s work. This is not meant to produce fear but honesty. God invites us to build with eternal materials: truth, love, humility, obedience, and service. What is built in Christ will last.

This passage invites us to examine the foundation and materials of our lives. Are we building on Christ? Are we investing in what will endure? God gives us grace to build carefully, faithfully, and with eternity in view.
devotionals.prayer: Dear Lord, please help me build my life on Christ alone. Teach me to use what is eternal, pure, and pleasing to You.

devotionals.title: You Belong to God
devotionals.scriptureText: All things are yours,  whether Paul or Apollos or Cephas[c] or the world or life or death or the present or the future—all are yours,  and you are of Christ, and Christ is of God. 1 Corinthians 3:21–23
devotionals.body:
In today’s passage, Apostle Paul lifts the Corinthians out of their small arguments and reminds them of their true identity. They had been dividing themselves around leaders, but Paul shows them that they already possess something far greater: they are God’s temple, God’s people, and Christ’s own. Their identity is not found in who they follow but in whom they belong to.

Here are three truths from today’s passage:

1. God’s Spirit lives among His people. Paul says, “You are God’s temple.” This is both personal and communal. The church is not ordinary. God Himself dwells among His people. Division, pride, and rivalry are serious because they damage what God has made holy.

2. Worldly wisdom cannot define spiritual reality. What the world calls wise may be foolish before God. Human systems often celebrate self-promotion, competition, and status. But God’s wisdom leads us toward humility, surrender, and dependence on Christ. We must be willing to become “fools” in the world’s eyes in order to become truly wise in God.

3. We do not belong to leaders; we belong to Christ. Paul turns their slogans upside down. They were saying, “I belong to Paul” or “I belong to Apollos.” Paul says all these servants are gifts for their good. They do not belong to the leaders. The leaders belong to them, and they belong to Christ.

This passage invites us to live from a place of belonging. We do not need to compete for identity or attach ourselves to personalities. We are God’s temple. We are Christ’s own. Everything finds its proper place when we remember whom we belong to.
devotionals.prayer: Dear Lord, thank You that I belong to You. Please free me from comparison and misplaced loyalty. Help me honor Your presence in me and in Your people.

devotionals.title: Faithful Stewards
devotionals.body:
In today’s passage, Apostle Paul invites the Corinthians to see Christian leadership through a different lens. He calls them to view every servant of Christ as a steward, someone entrusted with what belongs to another. A steward does not own the message, the gifts, or the ministry. Everything belongs to God. The one requirement is faithfulness.

Here are three truths from today’s passage:

1. We are servants entrusted with God’s gifts. Paul describes himself as a servant of Christ and a steward of the mysteries of God. Whatever God places in our hands is a trust. Our gifts, opportunities, influence, and responsibilities belong to Him. We are called to manage them with humility.

2. Faithfulness matters more than human approval. Paul refuses to let the opinions of others define his worth. Human judgment is limited. People see the surface, but God sees the heart. Our goal is not to please every voice but to be faithful to the One who called us.

3. God alone sees every motive clearly. Paul does not even trust his own self-assessment as final. The Lord will bring hidden things to light and reveal the motives of the heart. This truth humbles us and frees us. We do not need to expose, compare, or condemn others. God is the righteous Judge.

This passage invites us to live with a steward’s heart. We hold everything loosely, serve faithfully, and leave judgment to God. In the end, the praise that matters will come from Him.
devotionals.prayer: Dear Lord, please make me a faithful steward of what You’ve entrusted to me. Free me from the need for human approval and keep my motives pure before You.

devotionals.title: The Way of the Cross
devotionals.scriptureText: We work hard with our own hands. When we are cursed, we bless; when we are persecuted, we endure it; when we are slandered, we answer kindly. 1 Corinthians 4:12-13
devotionals.body:
In today’s passage, Apostle Paul confronts the pride that had grown in the Corinthian church. They were acting as though they had already arrived, already ruled, and already possessed everything they needed. Paul contrasts their self-satisfaction with the costly path of the apostles. The way of Christ is not self-exaltation but humility, endurance, and sacrificial love.

Here are three truths from today’s passage:

1. Pride forgets that everything is received. Paul asks, “What do you have that you did not receive?” Every gift, opportunity, and success comes from God. Boasting disappears when we remember that grace is the source of everything good in us.

2. The way of the cross often looks weak to the world. The apostles experienced hunger, hardship, dishonor, and rejection. Their lives did not fit the world’s picture of success. Yet their weakness revealed Christ’s strength. God’s kingdom often advances through people who are willing to be overlooked and misunderstood.

3. Christlike strength responds differently. When cursed, they blessed. When persecuted, they endured. When slandered, they answered kindly. This is the power of the cross at work in human relationships. Grace changes not only what we believe but how we respond when we are mistreated.

This passage invites us to embrace the way of the cross. To release pride, remember grace, and respond to hostility with the character of Christ. The world may call this weakness, but heaven calls it strength.
devotionals.prayer: Dear Lord, please teach me the way of the cross. Free me from pride and help me respond to others with humility, endurance, and grace.

devotionals.title: A Call to Imitate Christ
devotionals.body:
In today’s passage, Apostle Paul speaks to the Corinthians as a spiritual father who longs to see Christ formed in his children. Paul reminds them that the gospel is not only taught; it is demonstrated. He invites them to imitate his life because his life is shaped by Christ. This is a call to embodied discipleship.

Here are three truths from today’s passage:

1. Spiritual correction should flow from love. Paul does not write to shame them but to warn them as beloved children. Godly correction is not driven by embarrassment or control. It comes from a heart that wants others to grow into maturity.

2. The Christian life is learned through example. Paul says, “Imitate me.” He sends Timothy to remind them of his way of life in Christ. Truth becomes visible through people who live it. We need godly examples, and we are also becoming examples for others.

3. God’s kingdom is demonstrated by power, not empty talk. Some people were arrogant because they assumed Paul would not come. But Paul reminds them that the kingdom is not a matter of words but of power. The gospel produces real transformation, humility, holiness, and love.

This passage invites us to receive correction with humility and to live as examples of Christ. Our words should be matched by a life shaped by grace. The goal is not imitation of personality but imitation of Christlike character.
devotionals.prayer: Dear Lord, please surround me with people who walk in the way of Christ. Help me receive correction with humility and become an example of Your grace.

devotionals.title: A Call to Holy Love
devotionals.scriptureText: So when you are assembled and I am with you in spirit, and the power of our Lord Jesus is present, hand this man over to Satan for the destruction of the flesh, so that his spirit may be saved on the day of the Lord. 1 Corinthians 5:4-5
devotionals.body:
In today’s passage, Apostle Paul confronts serious sin within the Corinthian church. Their response had been prideful tolerance rather than grief. Paul calls them to act, not from cruelty, but from a desire for restoration. Holy love does not ignore what destroys people. It tells the truth, sets boundaries, and seeks redemption.

Here are three truths from today’s passage:

1. Sin should produce grief, not pride. The Corinthians had become proud of their tolerance. Paul says they should have mourned. When sin damages a person or a community, love does not celebrate or excuse it. Love grieves because it understands the cost of brokenness.

2. The church has a responsibility to protect holiness. Paul instructs the community to remove the unrepentant person from fellowship. This action is serious, but it is not revenge. The church must protect the health of the body and make clear that persistent rebellion is incompatible with life in Christ.

3. Discipline should aim at restoration. Paul’s hope is that the person’s spirit may be saved. Biblical discipline is not about destruction but rescue. It creates space for repentance and reminds the wandering person of the seriousness of returning to Christ.

This passage invites us to hold truth and love together. Holy love does not ignore sin, and holiness does not abandon people. God calls His church to respond with grief, courage, and a longing for restoration.
devotionals.prayer: Dear Lord, please give me a heart that grieves over sin and rejoices in restoration. Teach me to walk in truth, holiness, and love.

devotionals.title: New Life, New Way
devotionals.scriptureText: Get rid of the old yeast, so that you may be a new unleavened batch—as you really are. For Christ, our Passover lamb, has been sacrificed. 1 Corinthians 5:7
devotionals.body:
In today’s passage, Apostle Paul uses the image of yeast to show how a small amount of tolerated sin can influence an entire community. But he does not only tell the Corinthians what to remove. He reminds them who they already are. Christ, our Passover Lamb, has been sacrificed. Because of Him, we are a new people called to live in a new way.

Here are three truths from today’s passage:

1. Small compromises can spread. A little yeast works through the whole batch of dough. Sin that is ignored rarely stays contained. It shapes habits, relationships, and communities. God calls us to deal honestly with what threatens spiritual health.

2. Our new life is rooted in Christ’s sacrifice. Paul does not say, “Become a new batch.” He says, “as you really are.” Christ’s sacrifice has already created a new identity for us. We remove the old because it no longer matches who we are in Him.

3. The new life is marked by sincerity and truth. Paul contrasts the old yeast of malice and wickedness with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth. The Christian life is not performance. It is a life of integrity, where the heart and actions are aligned with Christ.

This passage invites us to live from our new identity. Christ has been sacrificed. The old life has lost its claim. We are called to remove what corrupts and celebrate the feast with sincerity, truth, and gratitude.
devotionals.prayer: Dear Lord, thank You that Christ has been sacrificed for me. Please remove every old pattern that does not reflect my new life in You.
